CURRICULUM VITAE

Tomislav Mesarić
Ulica Lipa 12, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia | +385 1 555 0142 | tomislav.mesaric@example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Butcher and meat-counter professional with nine years of experience in butchery and customer service. Skilled in breaking down beef, pork and lamb, boning, trimming, portioning and preparing fresh sausages. Experienced in FIFO stock rotation and HACCP-related temperature and hygiene checks, with practical knowledge of advising customers on cuts, quantities and cooking times.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Butcher | Mesnica Kod Ante, family butcher shop, Zagreb | 2019–present
• Break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides per week; bone, trim and portion meat for the service counter.
• Prepare around 40 kg of fresh sausages per week during the busy season, including ćevapi, kobasice, chipolata and lamb merguez.
• Developed the shop’s lamb merguez recipe and adjusted the ćevapi mix to 70% beef and 30% lamb following customer feedback; the ćevapi won second place at the 2023 Zagreb County craft meat fair.
• Rotate cold-room stock each morning using FIFO, placing older products at the front.
• Record cold-room (0–4 °C) and display-counter temperature checks twice daily.
• Serve about 120 customers on a Saturday, advising on cuts, quantities and cooking times.
• Prepare whole lambs and suckling pigs for spit-roasting orders, including weddings and family events.
• Conducted a six-week dry-ageing trial of beef ribs in 2024, recording temperature and weight loss; the shop now offers dry-aged rib by pre-order.
• Trained two apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines.

Counter Assistant | Tržnica Dolac meat hall stall, Zagreb | 2015–2019
• Served customers, weighed and priced orders, operated the till and completed cash-up.
• Cleaned and sanitised slicers, mincers and the counter at closing.
• Wrote a closing and cleaning checklist for the slicer, mincer, counter and floor drain following a market hygiene inspection remark.

EDUCATION & CERTIFICATES
Vocational Certificate: Butcher (3-year programme) | Food Trades School Zagreb | 2015
HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate | 2021; renewed 2024
Preparing for the Master Butcher exam (majstorski ispit), planned for spring 2027

SKILLS
Carcass breakdown (beef, pork and lamb) · Boning, trimming and portioning · Fresh sausage making · FIFO stock rotation · HACCP-related temperature and hygiene checks · Knife sharpening · Mincer and bandsaw operation · Customer service and advice on cuts and cooking · Fresh-meat packaging by paper wrapping · Cash handling

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native) · English (good) · German (basic)


COVER LETTER

Dear FreshCart Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at your Zagreb-Jarun store. I have completed butcher training and bring nine years of experience across butchery and meat-counter service, including carcass breakdown, customer advice and food-safety checks.

In my current butcher role at Mesnica Kod Ante, I break down beef and pork, bone and portion meat for the counter, and prepare fresh sausages. I rotate stock each morning using FIFO and record cold-room and display-counter temperatures twice daily. Previously, at the Dolac market meat stall, I served customers, weighed and priced orders, operated the till and maintained clean, sanitised equipment. These experiences match the role’s focus on fresh-meat preparation, well-managed stock, customer service and HACCP checks.

I take pride in giving practical advice on cuts, quantities and cooking times. I’m also drawn to FreshCart’s emphasis on product knowledge and honest customer advice through its “Ask the counter” promise. My experience developing the shop’s lamb merguez and refining its ćevapi recipe in response to customer feedback reflects the value I place on understanding products and listening to customers.

Mesnica Kod Ante is closing at the end of 2026 as its owner retires, so I am seeking my next role in butchery and meat-counter service. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to FreshCart’s counter team.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional and well tailored to FreshCart. It clearly explains the candidate's nine years of relevant experience, butcher training, customer service, FIFO rotation, temperature recording and sausage-making background. The paragraph connecting the candidate's product-development experience to FreshCart's “Ask the counter” promise is particularly effective. The closing explanation about the current shop closing is factual and gives a credible reason for seeking a new role. The letter could make the candidate's strongest quantified evidence more prominent, especially the volume of meat handled and Saturday customer service, but there are no major content or professionalism problems.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses ATS-friendly plain text structure, standard headings, readable paragraphs and relevant terms including “butcher training,” “carcass breakdown,” “fresh sausages,” “FIFO,” “temperature,” “HACCP,” “customer service,” and “cuts.” AI and ATS screening probability is high because the opening paragraph immediately establishes the required qualification and experience. For stronger keyword coverage, the letter could explicitly use the job ad's wording “completed butcher training,” “fresh-meat preparation,” “portion,” “package,” and “stock rotation” where supported. It should not claim experience with supermarket self-service packaging, tray sealers or labelling scales because those are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document strongly aligns with both must-have requirements: completed butcher training and HACCP knowledge. It also demonstrates the core duties of cutting and portioning meat, advising customers, rotating stock using FIFO, and recording temperature checks. The emphasis on practical product knowledge, honest advice and responding to customer feedback fits FreshCart's culture well. The candidate's lack of a forklift licence is a genuine nice-to-have gap, not a document defect. The candidate also has no stated supermarket experience and has not used tray sealers or self-service labelling scales; these are experience gaps rather than problems that should be disguised through wording. The letter appropriately avoids making unsupported claims about them.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the second paragraph, replace “I break down beef and pork, bone and portion meat for the counter, and prepare fresh sausages” with a more specific, keyword-rich sentence supported by the CV: “I break down beef, pork and lamb, bone, trim and portion meat for the service counter, and prepare approximately 40 kg of fresh sausage per week during the busy season.” This gives stronger evidence for the role's cutting and portioning requirements and uses the ad's “service counter” terminology.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the second paragraph, add the strongest customer-service evidence after the sentence about previous counter work: “In my current role, I serve approximately 120 customers on a Saturday and advise them on cuts, quantities and cooking times.” This directly mirrors the job's customer-advice requirement and makes the impact more concrete.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the opening paragraph, change “I have completed butcher training” to “I hold a completed three-year vocational certificate in Butchery and bring nine years of experience in butchery and meat-counter service.” This makes the formal qualification easier for ATS screening to identify while remaining fully supported by the candidate information.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “giving practical advice on cuts, quantities and cooking times”

In my current role, I serve approximately 120 customers on a Saturday and advise them on cuts, quantities and cooking times. These experiences match the role’s focus on fresh-meat preparation, well-managed stock, customer service and HACCP checks.

I’m also drawn to FreshCart’s emphasis on product knowledge and honest customer advice through its “Ask the counter” promise. My experience developing the shop’s lamb merguez and refining its ćevapi recipe in response to customer feedback reflects the value I place on understanding products and listening to customers.

Mesnica Kod Ante is closing at the end of 2026 as its owner retires, so I am seeking my next role in butchery and meat-counter service. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to FreshCart’s counter team.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional and well targeted to the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant role. It clearly establishes the candidate’s completed butcher training, nine years of relevant experience, carcass breakdown, fresh sausage production, FIFO stock rotation, temperature checks, customer service and HACCP-related work. The quantified examples—approximately 40 kg of sausage weekly and around 120 Saturday customers—add credibility and impact. The paragraph connecting the candidate’s product-development experience to FreshCart’s “Ask the counter” promise also shows genuine company alignment. The reason for leaving is transparent and professionally phrased. No unsupported skills or experience were identified.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses simple, readable formatting and standard section-free letter paragraphs that should parse reliably in ATS and AI screening systems. It includes strong job-related keywords such as butcher, meat-counter service, carcass breakdown, bone, trim, portion, fresh sausage, FIFO, temperature checks, HACCP, customer service and product knowledge. AI screening probability is high because the letter directly connects the candidate’s evidence to the advertised duties. A minor opportunity is to use the exact phrase “fresh-meat preparation” more prominently and explicitly mention “meat counter” alongside “service counter,” although the current wording is already highly searchable.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is excellent. The document shows the must-have completed butcher training and more than two years of meat-counter experience, as well as HACCP-related temperature and hygiene checks. It addresses the core duties of cutting, portioning, stock rotation, customer advice and counter service. The product knowledge, honest advice and customer-service culture are supported by the candidate’s experience advising customers on cuts, quantities and cooking times and responding to customer feedback when developing products. The candidate does not hold the nice-to-have forklift licence; this is a candidate gap rather than a document defect and should not be presented as a weakness in the letter. The candidate also lacks supermarket self-service packaging experience, but the job description does not list this as a stated requirement and the letter appropriately avoids claiming it.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT: In the second paragraph, change “These experiences match the role’s focus on fresh-meat preparation, well-managed stock, customer service and HACCP checks” to “These experiences match the role’s focus on fresh-meat preparation, cutting, portioning, FIFO stock rotation, customer advice and HACCP temperature and hygiene checks.” This uses more of the job advertisement’s terminology while remaining fully supported by the candidate’s experience.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT: In the opening paragraph, change “including carcass breakdown, customer advice and food-safety checks” to “including carcass breakdown, boning, trimming, portioning, customer advice and HACCP temperature and hygiene checks.” This makes the strongest role-specific skills more explicit for ATS and recruiter scanning.
